question_text: We replace 7.5 atomic percent of the chromium atoms in its BCC crystal with tantalum. X-ray diffraction shows that the lattice parameter is 0.29158 nm . Calculate the density of the alloy. Give your answer as as the value of density_g_per_cm3.The unit of the answer is g/cm³.
response:
For a BCC alloy, there are 2 atoms per unit cell. The alloy composition is 92.5 at% Cr and 7.5 at% Ta, so the average atomic weight is:

$$\bar{A} = 0.925(51.996) + 0.075(180.948) \approx 61.67 \text{ g/mol}$$

The unit cell volume is $a^3 = (0.29158\times10^{-7}\text{ cm})^3 \approx 2.479\times10^{-23}\text{ cm}^3$.

The density is:

$$\rho = \frac{n\bar{A}}{a^3 N_A} = \frac{2 \times 61.67}{(2.479\times10^{-23})(6.022\times10^{23})} \approx 8.26 \text{ g/cm}^3$$

$$\boxed{8.26}$$
